title: Rename in the UI wording
request: Reword the product frontend so 'contract' becomes 'solution' wherever it names the product's object: 'Draft the solution', 'Solution draft', 'Solution & data', the WF-01 node 'Solution'.
spec: The new wording across the 19 views, features.js and data.js. Done when a search for 'contract' in web/src finds only research wording and internal CSS class names.
plan: Reword about 200 occurrences across the views, features.js and data.js.
Keep quotes from research records, such as 'Decision-time contract' in dataset records, as written.
Review the visible labels and a sample of reworded sentences for awkward phrasing.
Rebuild with make web and check every page for leftover wording.
Search scripts and docs outside the package for old tool or route names.

decisions.decision: Internal CSS class names such as .contract-sheet stay.
decisions.why: They are invisible to users; renaming them with the CSS adds risk for no visible gain.

decisions.decision: The exact text 'Decision-time contract:' in research records is protected.
decisions.why: The Evidence page's parser looks for that string inside the real records; rewording it would break the parser.

change: The product frontend says solution wherever it names the product's object; research quotes and internal class names are unchanged; static/app rebuilt.
outcome: Done: the UI speaks of the solution. A later search found 'contract' only in the synthetic-data placeholder ('contract type', a telecom column in the example) and in research wording, both correct as they are.
lessons: After a wording rename, search again whenever new screens are added, and read each hit in context: a dataset's own column named 'contract' is not the product's object.
